plan.lspNative.title: Native LSP and completion workflow
plan.lspNative.description: Checks real NVDA output, held Braille information, and perceptible menu interaction; LSP content and event sequences already have automated coverage.
plan.lspNative.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. The Python file lsp_features.py is open. Press Escape once; you are then in Normal mode and cannot insert stray characters.
plan.lspNative.status.title: Report the active LSP clearly
plan.lspNative.status.action: After claiming with F12, press F1, wait for all NVDA speech, then press Escape and F10.
plan.lspNative.status.expected: NVDA clearly reports that Pyright is active for the Python buffer. It does not expose a raw Lua or protocol representation.
plan.lspNative.parameters.title: Hold function parameters on Braille
plan.lspNative.parameters.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. The cursor is already on the function name calculate_total. Press Escape once and do not move the cursor.
plan.lspNative.parameters.action: After claiming with F12, hold NVDA, briefly press Shift+P, and release only Shift+P. Keep NVDA held: verify that only signature 1 with its documentation appears first, then use the display's normal forward/back controls to page once through that information and return to its start. Slowly press l three times and h twice; the first press must show parameter 1, the later presses move through parameters 2 and 3 and back to parameter 1. Press j once and verify that only signature 2 with its documentation appears. Press l three times: here too, the first press must show parameter 1 before parameters 2 and 3 follow. Press k once: signature 1 must appear without a parameter; a following l must first show its last selected parameter 1 and must neither skip it nor use a parameter from signature 2. Release NVDA and repeat the same held query once without moving the cursor. Then release NVDA and press Escape and F10.
plan.lspNative.parameters.expected: Speech says signature, parameter, and documentation in full. On Braille, signatures start compactly with S 1 of 2 or S 2 of 2, parameters with P 1 of 3 through P 3 of 3, and documentation with D:. The calculate_total function name and the price, quantity, and discount parameter names remain complete. The initial view and j/k show only the selected signature with documentation; h/l shows only one of its parameters. After the initial view and every signature change, the first h or l press shows the parameter selected for that signature without immediately skipping it. Both signatures start independently at parameter 1 without mixing their parameter positions. Paging keeps the current signature information on the Braille display; source text returns only after NVDA is released. The immediate repeated query makes the same information available again.
plan.lspNative.completion.title: Operate and perceive native completion
plan.lspNative.completion.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. Press Escape once. F3 moves to a prepared completion location and enters Insert mode automatically.
plan.lspNative.completion.action: After claiming with F12, press F3 and then F5. Continue with Ctrl+N beyond calculate_total, calculate_tax, and calculate_tip: after the last candidate, reach the state with no selected completion once, then candidate 1 on the next press. Move back at least once with Ctrl+P and accept one suggestion with Ctrl+Y. If audio was answered Yes at startup, also listen for the opening sound and the distinct closing sound caused by acceptance. Then press Escape and F10.
plan.lspNative.completion.expected: The menu contains at least the three prepared suggestions calculate_total, calculate_tax, and calculate_tip. NVDA reports selected suggestions clearly. The step between the last and first candidate explicitly reports that no completion is selected; it is not silent. Navigation and acceptance respond smoothly and without disruptive repetition. When audio is available, menu open and menu close each sound exactly once and are clearly distinct; without declared audio, only the other perception is assessed.
plan.diagnostics.title: Diagnostic output and earcons
plan.diagnostics.description: Checks perceptible Ruff diagnostics, navigation, sounds, and physical Braille persistence. Ranges, sources, and jump targets also have automated coverage.
plan.diagnostics.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. diagnostics.py is open and the cursor is already on the unused import path on line one; sep on the same line is unused as well. Press Escape once and do not move the cursor yet.
plan.diagnostics.navigation.title: Speak, navigate, and perceive diagnostics
plan.diagnostics.navigation.action: After claiming with F12, press F6 and wait until “Diagnostics ready” is announced. Only then press F7; it reports the Ruff F401 warning at the cursor. Slowly press F9 repeatedly and follow “number of total” until the Ruff F821 error for missing_name and, after the last diagnostic, the first one are reached. Press F8 once to move backwards to the last diagnostic. If audio was answered Yes at startup, compare the warning and error sounds. Then press Escape and F10.
plan.diagnostics.navigation.expected: F7 clearly reports a diagnostic for the unused import. F9 reaches every announced number, including multiple diagnostics at the same position, and then wraps to the first; F8 moves backwards to the last. Every key press produces exactly one complete announcement without disruptive delay. When audio is available, F401 uses the warning sound and F821 the clearly different error sound; each jump produces exactly one diagnostic sound without disruptive overlap. Without declared audio, only the other perception is assessed. Together with completion, all four distinct sounds are covered when audio is available: menu open, menu close, warning, and error.
plan.diagnostics.held.title: Hold a diagnostic on Braille
plan.diagnostics.held.action: After claiming with F12, press F6, wait for “Diagnostics ready”, and only then press F7. Next hold NVDA, briefly press Shift+E, and release only Shift+E. Keep NVDA held, press j once and then k once to switch between the F401 diagnostics for path and sep and back. Finally release NVDA, then press Escape and F10.
plan.diagnostics.held.expected: The two distinct F401 diagnostics for path and sep are readable on Braille while the gesture is held and change with j/k. Releasing it restores the previous Braille output.
plan.focus.title: Focus isolation and fail-open behavior
plan.focus.description: Checks actual Windows Terminal ownership and return to normal terminal behavior, which test doubles cannot reproduce completely.
plan.focus.workflow.title: Distinguish claimed and unclaimed terminal tabs
plan.focus.context: You initially are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. Press Escape, claim exactly this tab with F12, and leave Neovim open. The middle part needs a second Windows Terminal tab showing an ordinary PowerShell prompt.
plan.focus.workflow.action: Use the plus button or profile menu to open a second Windows Terminal tab with PowerShell. Do not start Neovim or press F12 there. Check ordinary input and navigation without submitting a command. Return to the original tab, press Escape and F10 in Neovim, then check ordinary input and navigation again in the PowerShell view that reappears there.
plan.focus.workflow.expected: The second unclaimed tab keeps NVDA's normal terminal behavior and receives no Neovim output from the first tab. After F10, PowerShell in the original tab is immediately usable normally as well; no Braille output is stuck and input is not blocked.
plan.completionPlugin.context: You are in the test Neovim in the original Windows Terminal tab. The Python file is open. Press Escape once. F3 moves to a prepared completion location and enters Insert mode automatically.
plan.nvimCmp.title: Optional nvim-cmp compatibility
plan.nvimCmp.description: A short reality check of the automatically tested adapter API with NVDA and Windows Terminal.
plan.nvimCmp.menu.title: Operate and perceive nvim-cmp suggestions
plan.nvimCmp.menu.action: After claiming with F12, press F3 and F5, select at least calculate_total, calculate_tax, and calculate_tip with Ctrl+N, move back with Ctrl+P, and accept with Ctrl+Y. If audio was answered Yes at startup, also listen for the opening sound and the distinct closing sound caused by acceptance. Then press Escape and F10.
plan.nvimCmp.menu.expected: The menu contains at least the three prepared suggestions. NVDA clearly reports selected nvim-cmp suggestions; navigation and acceptance remain smooth, and internal tables are not spoken. When audio is available, opening and closing each produce exactly one suitable, distinct menu sound; without declared audio, only the other perception is assessed.
